items.title: Rethinking the user interface of AI, open source<3
items.raw_excerpt: Hi everyone, I've spent the last year using tools like NotebookLM and ChatGPT for stuff ranging from studying, research, and writing. Its been okay, but I've found that this standard chat interface has been a bottleneck for sustained work. The answers are useful, but all of the information remain limited in linear, ephemeral threads than would also span across multiple conversations. ThinkEx is an open-source alternative that augments the normal the chat interface with a spatial, grid-like canvas. It works like a physical desk: instead of your context scrolling away or getting lost across different windows, you spread out PDFs, videos, and notes side-by-side to interact them easily. Its fully open source as well :)

excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past decade, the market's vision of "AI assistants" has undergone three major rounds of expectation calibration. The first was with the birth of Siri, where voice control brought a novelty in interaction, leading people to believe that the intelligent butler Jarvis from movies was within reach, only to later find it was often just a voice-activated alarm clock. The second was the emergence of ChatGPT, whose fluent conversation and reasoning abilities made it seem like AI had finally gained a "brain," but the market soon realized it remained merely a sage confined to dialog boxes, unaware of the world beyond. In early 2025, the appearance of Manus gave tangible reality to the concept of an Agent. This impact was different from before—many saw for the first time that AI was not only "talking" but also "doing." It opened browsers, wrote code, debugged errors right before your eyes, and even proactively refreshed pages when loading was too slow. As the hype around Manus gradually subsided following its acquisition, people realized that, regardless of how the technological shell evolves, humanity's core desire for AI assistants has never changed: users don't just want a chat companion that merely understands speech, nor do they only want a geek tool that writes code in a black-and-white interface; what everyone has always wanted is...
excerpt_i18n.es: En los últimos diez años, el mercado ha experimentado tres grandes ajustes de expectativas sobre la imaginación de los "asistentes de IA". La primera fue con el nacimiento de Siri, donde el control por voz trajo una novedad en la interacción, haciendo creer que el mayordomo inteligente Jarvis de las películas estaba al alcance, pero pronto se descubrió que en la mayoría de los casos solo era un despertador de voz. La segunda ocurrió con la aparición de ChatGPT, cuya fluidez en el diálogo y capacidad de razonamiento hicieron pensar que la IA finalmente tenía "cerebro", pero rápidamente el mercado se dio cuenta de que seguía siendo solo una inteligencia que debatía en un cuadro de diálogo.
